check1.set: open-door gas-burner tests of nominal 250 or 500 kW (above 100 kW)
check1.steadyPeriod: from the events file's Ignition to its Burner Off (the file's Time column is seconds from Ignition; checked: the row at Time 0 carries Ignition's clock time); every 1 s reading with 0 <= t < Burner Off, as recorded (no lag shift, no pre-ignition baseline taken off)

aside100kW.note: nominal 100 kW: outside 15.5's set (above 100 kW); kept apart, not in any summary

check2.plan: fire-calibration-plan-2026-11-11.md, section 15.3 (the FSRI part; NIST's Fire Calorimetry Database not read here)
check2.set: open-door upholstered chair tests (RedAccent: the README's Red Accent Chair; Overstuffed: the README's Overstuffed Sofa, the plan's overstuffed chair)
check2.readings: the suite's 5 s means of the 1 s record (each the mean of the readings in (s - 2.5, s + 2.5], s = 0, 5, 10 ... s from Ignition), for the peak, the window and the fit
check2.window: from the first 5 s mean above 25 kW (t >= 0) to the first at 90 % of the 5 s peak, both included
check2.fit: least squares of q = alpha max(0, t - t0)^2, t0 free (scanned in 0.5 s steps over [window start - 1200 s, window end), refined by golden section)
check2.energy: the 1 s readings summed from Ignition to the record's end (kJ to MJ), and to the Suppression event; no baseline taken off
check2.massSource: 02_Info/furniture_mass.csv (initial mass only; no mass-loss record exists in the series, so the energy is not recomputed from mass loss)
